column3: The `ln -s . l` operand needs Windows Developer Mode; without it the symlink does not exist and df reports l missing (rc 1), while GNU resolves the symlink to its mount and prints the table (rc 0). Platform-bound symlink creation, recorded not gated. Round-2 re-probe: this host has Developer Mode OFF (HKLM AppModelUnlock absent), so the Windows sides still see rc 1 — premise intact.

`--reference=f g` applies the referenced file's owner to g. GNU runs as root and applies it silently (rc 0); the Windows sides cannot carry out the owner change through the OS (no root/SeTakeOwnership equivalent in the gate context) and report the failure rc 1. OS-privilege-bound, recorded not gated; note masks a live rc divergence (MASKED-DIVERGENCE class — command lane owns the fix or re-justification).

`chown -h 0 s` changes the symlink's own owner. GNU (root) sets it rc 0; on Windows the numeric owner of a symlink cannot be set without privilege AND the scratch symlink needs Developer Mode to exist at all — the Windows sides fail rc 1 (with Dev Mode off the symlink is never created, so chown reports it missing). Platform/privilege-bound, recorded not gated; MASKED-DIVERGENCE class.

`-v :5678 f` succeeds on both sides (rc 0) but the verbose line is worded differently: GNU prints "changed group of 'f' from root to 5678", the Windows side prints the ownership-of form with the platform's account rendering. rc parity holds, stdout platform-form-bound — exit-mode contract; note kept until the command lane promotes it (UPGRADE-EXIT).

`-v 1234 f` succeeds on both sides (rc 0); GNU prints "changed ownership of 'f' from root to 1234", the Windows side prints "ownership of 'f' retained as 1234". rc parity holds, stdout platform-form-bound — exit-mode contract; promotion owned by the command lane (UPGRADE-EXIT).

`hostid -h` (round-2 re-probe): GNU reports the invalid short option on stderr ("hostid: invalid option -- 'h'" + Try line) and exits 1; the rust2 hostid treats -h silently rc 0 — live rc divergence under the note (MASKED-DIVERGENCE class: hostid's option surface predates argopt and has no invalid-option diagnostic).

`ln -s tgt sl` needs Windows Developer Mode (unprivileged symlink creation). With Dev Mode ON the round-1 sweep matched GNU byte-for-byte (UPGRADE-STRICT — promotion owned by the command lane); with Dev Mode OFF (this host at round 2) CreateSymbolicLinkW fails "Operation not permitted" and the Windows sides exit 1 while GNU creates the link rc 0. Environment-bound, recorded not gated.

`ln -sf tgt pre` must replace the existing symlink; replacement goes through the same CreateSymbolicLinkW path as ln22, so the whole case inherits the Developer Mode bound (Dev Mode off: rc 1 Operation not permitted; Dev Mode on: matched GNU rc 0). Environment-bound, recorded not gated.

`ln -s dd sldd` (symlink to a directory) — same Developer Mode bound as ln22-s; the target being a directory adds nothing on the Windows symlink API. Dev Mode off: rc 1; round-1 Dev-Mode-on sweep matched GNU byte-for-byte (UPGRADE-STRICT). Environment-bound.

`ln -b -s tgt bt` (backup + symlink): the -b backup path is exercised only after the symlink is created, so the case inherits the ln22 Developer Mode bound (Dev Mode off: rc 1 before any backup happens; Dev Mode on: matched GNU). Environment-bound.

`stat -c %C reg` asks for the SELinux security context. No Windows side provides one, so every side prints the GNU "?" placeholder; GNU exits 1 because the context is unavailable, and the rust2 stat matches that rc 1 byte-for-byte (round-2 UPGRADE-STRICT: rust rc 1 + "?\n" == GNU). Only the 1.x C++ body's historic rc varies. Note kept until the command lane promotes the row.

GNU test has no --help flag: the sole argument "--help" is a non-empty string operand, so it is silently true (rc 0, no output). The rust2 test follows GNU byte-for-byte (round-2 UPGRADE-STRICT); the 1.x C++ body prints a usage screen instead (deviation inherited-not-fixed, recorded via r=c). Promotion owned by the command lane.

`users -h` (round-2 re-probe): GNU reports "users: invalid option -- 'h'" + Try line on stderr and exits 1; the rust2 users treats -h silently rc 0 — live rc divergence under the note (MASKED-DIVERGENCE class: same missing invalid-short-option diagnostic as hostid ho12).
